newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends slightly down, trading dull.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends slightly down, trading dull.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed slightly lower in continued dull trading as buyers remained largely sidelined, traders said.
"Nothing was done all day. Buyers are still nowhere to be seen," said one local dealer, expecting activity to stay quiet through the week.
"Prices are likely to stay flat this week," the dealer said.

Traders said local prices were currently held by sellers' reserve, technical adjustment and steady prices in Thailand due to support from the government. "If Thai prices start falling again, we may follow," the dealer added.
At the close, mew spot position April RSS1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 302 cents ($1.22) a kg, unchanged from Friday.
April SMR 20 buyer was down half cent at 298 cents ($1.20).
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 294 cents a kg, SMR CV at 358, SMR L at 338, SMR 5 at 305, SMR 10 at 295 and drum latex FOB at 237.
The INRO five-day moving average was 231.54 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Feb 28 against 231.70 on Feb 27. The daily indicator price was 231.80 versus 231.57.
